QuestionStmt.S: The value of $$\frac{(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^4}{(\sin \theta + i \cos \theta)^5} =$$ where $i = \sqrt{-1}$

Solution.S:
$$\frac{(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^4}{(\sin \theta + i \cos \theta)^5} = \frac{(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^4}{i^5 (\cos \theta - i \sin \theta)^5}$$

Since $\sin \theta + i \cos \theta = i(\cos \theta - i \sin \theta)$ and $i^5 = i$.

$$= \frac{(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^4}{i (\cos \theta - i \sin \theta)^5}$$

Using $\cos \theta - i \sin \theta = (\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^{-1}$:

$$= \frac{(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^4}{i (\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^{-5}} = \frac{1}{i} (\cos \theta + i \sin \theta)^9$$

$$= -i (\cos 9\theta + i \sin 9\theta) = \sin 9\theta - i \cos 9\theta$$

Thus the correct option is D.
